title: Mathematics-1
syllabus: Calculus: mean value theorems, Taylor series, curve tracing; calculus of several variables, partial derivatives, maxima/minima, Lagrange multipliers; vector calculus: multiple integrals, gradient, divergence, curl, Green/Gauss/Stokes theorems; ordinary differential equations.
objectives: Apply single- and multi-variable calculus and solve ordinary differential equations.

title: Mathematics-II
syllabus: Linear algebra: vector spaces, subspaces, span, linear independence, basis and dimension, linear transformations, rank and nullity, matrices of linear maps, elementary row operations and solution of linear systems, eigenvalues; further topics in calculus and transforms.
objectives: Reason about vector spaces, linear maps and matrices and solve linear systems.

title: Introduction to Programming and Data Structures
syllabus: Computer fundamentals and algorithms; constants, variables, data types, operators and expressions; input-output; branching and iteration; functions and recursion; arrays and strings; structures and pointers; linked lists, stacks and queues; searching and sorting.
objectives: Write, test and debug structured programs and use basic data structures.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Introduction to Programming and Data Structures Laboratory
syllabus: Programs on expression evaluation, conditionals, iteration, functions, recursion, arrays, string manipulation, structures, linked lists and doubly linked lists.
objectives: Implement and debug small programs in a lab setting.
prerequisite_text: Introduction to Programming and Data Structures
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: English for Communication
syllabus: Literature (prose and poetry from the 16th century to the post-modern period), language and grammar, and communication: listening, speaking, reading and writing skills for academic and professional contexts.
objectives: Communicate clearly in speech and writing and read critically.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Physics
syllabus: Classical mechanics (Lagrangian and Hamiltonian), oscillations and waves, special relativity, electromagnetic waves and optics, and wave mechanics.
objectives: Apply classical, wave and quantum physics to engineering problems.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Chemistry
syllabus: Energetics and kinetics, equilibrium, redox and electrochemistry, bonding models and spectroscopy, functional materials, industrial and bio-inspired chemistry.
objectives: Use chemical principles to explain materials and energy systems.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Mechanics
syllabus: Force systems and equilibrium, friction, kinematics and kinetics of particles, properties of areas, stress and strain, torsion, bending, combined loading and column buckling.
objectives: Analyse forces, motion and stresses in simple structures.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Electrical Technology
syllabus: Sources of energy and power systems; DC networks: Kirchhoff's laws, node and mesh analysis, network theorems; AC circuits; magnetic circuits, transformers and electrical machines.
objectives: Analyse DC/AC circuits and basic electrical machines.
verification_note: First-year common course; section groups take it in Autumn or Spring (booklet p.5).

title: Introduction to Electronics
syllabus: Electronic devices: diodes, BJT and MOSFET; diode circuits, rectifiers; transistor biasing and amplifiers; operational amplifiers and their applications.
objectives: Analyse basic electronic devices and amplifier circuits.

title: Introduction to Bio Science and Technology
syllabus: Cell as the unit of life; genes, DNA and bioinformatics; proteins and enzymes; overview of biotechnology applications.
objectives: Explain core biological concepts relevant to engineering.

title: Discrete Structures
syllabus: Set theory, induction and Peano postulates; relations, equivalence relations and partial orders; countable and uncountable sets; propositional and predicate logic; combinatorics and recurrences; graphs and trees; algebraic structures.
objectives: Construct proofs and reason with sets, relations, logic, combinatorics and graphs.

title: Data Structures
syllabus: Applications of stacks, queues and linked lists; trees and traversals; binary search trees, AVL, 2-4, red-black and B-trees; dictionaries and hashing; tries and suffix trees; comparison sorting and lower bounds; priority queues and heaps; graphs.
objectives: Choose, implement and analyse data structures for a problem.

title: Signals and Systems
syllabus: Signal and system classification; LTI systems, impulse response and convolution; Fourier series and Fourier transform; Laplace and z-transforms; sampling.
objectives: Analyse signals and LTI systems in time and frequency domains.

title: Introduction to Electronics Laboratory
syllabus: Electronic components and instruments; frequency response of RC/RL networks; diode characteristics and rectifiers; transistor amplifiers.
objectives: Build and measure basic electronic circuits.

title: Signals and Systems Laboratory
syllabus: MATLAB programming with vectors and matrices, plotting, signal generation, convolution and Fourier analysis experiments.
objectives: Simulate and visualise signals with MATLAB.

title: Data Structures Laboratory
syllabus: Two-way stacks, deques, priority queues, sorting algorithms, dictionary structures for strings, cycle detection, BST and AVL applications.
objectives: Implement data structures and measure their behaviour.

title: Environmental Science Technology and Management
syllabus: Environmental science, pollution, resources and environmental management (syllabus published by the offering school; title, code, L-T-P and credits from the CSE semester IV table).
objectives: Explain environmental systems and management approaches.
verification_note: Syllabus not in the CSE booklet; only the table entry was verified.

title: Combinatorics, Probability and Statistics
syllabus: Counting and combinatorics, probability, random variables and distributions, expectation, limit theorems, estimation and hypothesis testing (syllabus published by the School of Basic Sciences; title, code and credits from the CSE semester IV table).
objectives: Model uncertainty and draw statistical inferences from data.
verification_note: Booklet table prints 'Combinatory, Probability and Statistics'; syllabus is published by the offering school.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
syllabus: Growth functions, recurrences, Master theorem and amortised analysis; divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, branch and bound, backtracking; graph algorithms: DFS, BFS, topological sort, shortest paths, spanning trees, flows; NP-completeness.
objectives: Design efficient algorithms and prove their correctness and complexity.
prerequisite_text: Programming and Data Structures, Data Structure

title: Digital Electronic Circuits
syllabus: Logic gates; Boolean algebra and minimisation (K-map, Quine-McCluskey); number systems and codes; combinational circuits; flip-flops, counters and registers; logic families.
objectives: Design combinational and sequential digital circuits.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms Laboratory
syllabus: Implementations of sorting, matrix multiplication, trees, graph traversals, shortest paths and network flows, measuring running time across input sets.
objectives: Implement algorithms and compare measured and predicted running time.

title: Digital Electronic Circuits Laboratory
syllabus: Logic gates, adders, multiplexers, comparators, encoders, multivibrators, flip-flops and counters.
objectives: Build and test digital circuits.

title: Project Seminar
syllabus: Literature survey on a chosen topic, technical report and seminar presentation under faculty guidance.
objectives: Survey literature on a topic and present it clearly.
verification_note: Code and credits from the semester IV table; content described from the course type.

title: Formal Languages and Automata Theory
syllabus: DFA, NFA and their equivalence; regular expressions, pumping lemma and closure properties; context-free grammars, pushdown automata and normal forms; Turing machines, decidability and undecidability.
objectives: Classify languages and reason about computability.

title: Computer Organization and Architecture
syllabus: Computer organisation and buses; assembly and machine language; instruction cycles; CPU organisation and instruction sets; control unit design; pipelining; memory hierarchy and cache; I/O and interrupts.
objectives: Explain how programs execute on hardware and evaluate architectural trade-offs.

title: Operating Systems
syllabus: Process concept and life cycle; threads; CPU scheduling; process synchronisation and deadlocks; memory management, paging and virtual memory; file systems; I/O and disk scheduling; protection.
objectives: Explain and apply OS mechanisms for processes, memory and storage.

title: Computer Organization and Architecture Laboratory
syllabus: Assembly language programming, synthesis of simple data paths and controllers, processor design, interfacing with DAC/ADC and keyboard-display modules.
objectives: Program at the assembly level and design simple datapaths.

title: Operating Systems Laboratory
syllabus: UNIX system calls for process management and inter-process communication; experiments on process scheduling and other OS tasks by simulation.
objectives: Use system calls and simulate OS policies.
verification_note: Syllabus header lists 2 credits; the semester V total implies 3. Using the syllabus value.

title: Database Systems
syllabus: Database system architecture and data models; ER modelling; relational model and algebra; SQL; functional dependencies and normalisation; storage and indexing; query processing; transactions, concurrency control and recovery.
objectives: Design normalised schemas and write correct, efficient SQL.

title: Computer Networks
syllabus: Goals of networking and layered architecture (OSI and Internet); data link: framing, error control, MAC; network layer: addressing and routing; transport: UDP and TCP, congestion control; application protocols: DNS, HTTP, e-mail.
objectives: Explain and analyse Internet protocols layer by layer.

title: Database Systems Laboratory
syllabus: Schema design, SQL creation, update and querying, PL/SQL, stored procedures, triggers and views on a commercial RDBMS.

title: Computer Networks Laboratory

verification_note: Syllabus header lists 2 credits; the semester VI total implies 3. Using the syllabus value.

title: Compiler Design
syllabus: Phases of compilation; lexical analysis with finite automata; parsing: top-down and bottom-up, LR parsers; syntax-directed translation; type checking; intermediate code; runtime environments; code generation and optimisation.
objectives: Build the front end of a compiler and explain code generation.
prerequisite_text: Programming and Data Structures, Formal Languages and Automata Theory

title: Compiler Design Laboratory
